cases.exposure_context_quote: The youngest sibling was exposed to paraquat following scalp application after complete shaving of the hair as part of a home remedy for head lice.
cases.agent_quote: The substance, obtained from an agricultural supply outlet and dispensed into a tied nylon sachet, was identified by the caregivers as “Gamaline 20,” a paraquat-containing herbicide.
cases.route: dermal (scalp application on freshly shaved, abraded scalp)
cases.circumstance: Home remedy for head lice: chemical applied directly onto freshly shaved scalp; not washed off; no immediate medical care sought before presentation.

symptoms.finding: sudden severe respiratory distress with hypoxemia
symptoms.quote: Approximately 36 h later, the child developed sudden onset severe respiratory distress, and was brought to the emergency department. On arrival, she was conscious but in marked respiratory distress with hypoxemia.

symptoms.finding: scalp abrasions, excoriations and ulcerative lesions
symptoms.quote: Physical examination revealed multiple scalp abrasions, excoriations and ulcerative lesions.
Her condition deteriorated rapidly within minutes, progressing to cardiorespiratory collapse.

treatment.name: immediate resuscitation, airway support and advanced life support
treatment.quote: Despite immediate resuscitative efforts, including airway support and advanced life support measures, she suffered cardiac arrest and died shortly after presentation.

cases.icu_admission: No (died shortly after presentation; 'Laboratory investigations were not performed due to the rapid progression.')
cases.outcome_quote: Despite immediate resuscitative efforts, including airway support and advanced life support measures, she suffered cardiac arrest and died shortly after presentation.
cases.notes: Youngest sibling with more extensive scalp injury; laboratory investigations not performed due to rapid progression.

cases.exposure_context_quote: The second sibling presented at the same time with mild respiratory symptoms and initially stable vital signs.
cases.agent_quote: The substance, obtained from an agricultural supply outlet and dispensed into a tied nylon sachet, was identified by the caregivers as “Gamaline 20,” a paraquat-containing herbicide.
cases.route: dermal (scalp application on shaved, abraded scalp)
cases.circumstance: Same exposure event as siblings: paraquat-containing herbicide applied to freshly shaved scalp as home remedy for head lice.

symptoms.finding: mild cough, throat irritation, early respiratory discomfort
symptoms.quote: She was conscious and oriented at presentation, with complaints of mild cough, throat irritation, and early respiratory discomfort.

symptoms.finding: oliguria with rising serum creatinine (acute kidney injury)
symptoms.quote: Within the first 24 h of hospitalization, she developed oliguria with rising serum creatinine, consistent with acute kidney injury.

symptoms.finding: worsening tachypnoea and declining oxygen saturation
symptoms.quote: This was followed by worsening tachypnoea and declining oxygen saturation, necessitating admission to the intensive care unit (ICU).

symptoms.finding: scalp abrasions, excoriations, shallow ulcerative lesions
symptoms.quote: Scalp examination showed complete hair shaving with multiple superficial abrasions, excoriated areas, and shallow ulcerative lesions, some with mild serous discharge

cases.time_to_care: Approximately 36 h after exposure (presented at the same time as siblings)

labs.name: serum creatinine (day 1)
labs.quote: For the 6-year-old, admission values showed markedly elevated serum creatinine (290 µmol/L, (reference range 35–90 µmol/L)) and urea (11.6 mmol/L (reference range 2.5–6.5 mmol/L)) with mild electrolyte imbalance and metabolic acidosis.

labs.name: urea (day 1)
labs.quote: For the 6-year-old, admission values showed markedly elevated serum creatinine (290 µmol/L, (reference range 35–90 µmol/L)) and urea (11.6 mmol/L (reference range 2.5–6.5 mmol/L)) with mild electrolyte imbalance and metabolic acidosis.

treatment.name: haemodialysis (two sessions, days 3 and 6)
treatment.quote: Each child underwent two sessions of haemodialysis (on days 3 and 6 of admission), which resulted in transient biochemical improvement

treatment.name: corticosteroids (intravenous hydrocortisone)
treatment.quote: Systemic corticosteroid therapy was instituted using intravenous hydrocortisone, in the absence of methylprednisolone, with the aim of attenuating pulmonary inflammation and limiting progression to fibrosis.

treatment.name: oxygen therapy and ventilatory support
treatment.quote: Both patients required escalating oxygen therapy due to worsening hypoxemia and progressive respiratory compromise.

treatment.name: maintenance intravenous fluids and electrolyte correction
treatment.quote: Maintenance intravenous fluids were administered using 5% dextrose-based solutions, with careful titration to avoid fluid overload while maintaining adequate perfusion. Electrolyte imbalances were corrected as required.

cases.icu_admission: Yes (admitted to the intensive care unit)
cases.outcome: Died on the ninth day of hospitalization from progressive respiratory failure
cases.outcome_quote: The 6-year-old child died on the ninth day of admission from progressive respiratory failure
cases.notes: Serial labs in Table 1; baseline oxygen saturation 88–92% on room air.

cases.exposure_context_quote: The eldest sibling also presented at the same time after paraquat exposure via scalp application.
cases.agent_quote: The substance, obtained from an agricultural supply outlet and dispensed into a tied nylon sachet, was identified by the caregivers as “Gamaline 20,” a paraquat-containing herbicide.
cases.route: dermal (scalp application on shaved, abraded scalp)
cases.circumstance: Same exposure event as siblings: paraquat-containing herbicide applied after scalp shaving as home remedy for head lice.

symptoms.quote: At admission, she was fully conscious and initially appeared clinically stable, although she reported mild respiratory symptoms similar to her siblings.

symptoms.finding: acute kidney injury with rising creatinine and reduced urine output
symptoms.quote: Over the subsequent days, she developed acute kidney injury, evidenced by rising serum creatinine levels and reduced urine output, necessitating admission to the ICU and initiation of haemodialysis.
Her respiratory status progressively worsened, with increasing oxygen requirements and persistent hypoxemia.
She subsequently developed multi-organ failure dominated by severe respiratory compromise
Examination of the scalp revealed recent shaving with widespread excoriations, superficial abrasions, and small ulcerated areas

cases.time_to_care: Approximately 36 h after exposure (presented at the same time as siblings)

labs.name: serum creatinine (day 1)
labs.quote: Similarly, the 8-year-old had elevated serum creatinine (325 µmol/L) and urea (12.5 mmol/L), with comparable electrolyte findings (Table 1, Table 2).

labs.name: urea (day 1)
labs.quote: Similarly, the 8-year-old had elevated serum creatinine (325 µmol/L) and urea (12.5 mmol/L), with comparable electrolyte findings (Table 1, Table 2).

treatment.name: haemodialysis (two sessions, days 3 and 6)
treatment.quote: Each child underwent two sessions of haemodialysis (on days 3 and 6 of admission), which resulted in transient biochemical improvement

treatment.name: corticosteroids and ventilatory support
treatment.quote: Despite aggressive supportive therapy, including corticosteroids and ventilatory support, her condition continued to deteriorate (Table 1, Table 2; Fig. 1, Fig. 2).

treatment.name: oxygen supplementation and supportive care
treatment.quote: the two older siblings were commenced on aggressive supportive therapy, including close monitoring of vital parameters, cautious oxygen supplementation to avoid risk of oxygen-enhanced oxidative injury, and correction of fluid and electrolyte abnormalities.

cases.outcome: Died on the tenth day of hospitalization following multi-organ failure
cases.outcome_quote: She subsequently developed multi-organ failure dominated by severe respiratory compromise and succumbed to the effects of paraquat toxicity on the tenth day of hospitalization.
cases.notes: Serial labs in Table 2; diagnosis supported by exposure history and container identification; no quantitative paraquat measurements available.
